feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader with clear public-sector specialization and solid evidence of progression and scope. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense, slightly repetitive across skills sections, and could sharpen impact by quantifying more outcomes beyond activity and scale.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong career progression within NACo and a well-defined niche in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and communications systems.  
- Good credibility signals: specific platforms, tools, audience scale, website size, and recent project examples make the profile feel substantive and believable.  
- Writing quality is strong: polished, concise, and consistent in tone; no obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to save space and improve scannability.  
- Add more outcome metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more results would strengthen impact (e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, conversion, cost/time savings).  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation style varies in lists; “English (Native) French (A2/Learning)” would read better with separators or bullets.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. Tightening it and adding one concrete scale cue would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad phrasing with a sharper value proposition, e.g.: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years driving web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations.”
- Add one concrete scale marker from recent experience to increase credibility, such as “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Simplify the second sentence by grouping related areas: “Leads enterprise web platforms, editorial systems, analytics infrastructure, multimedia operations, and AI-enabled search/content experiences.”
- Use “drives” or “delivers” instead of “leads” if you want a more active, outcome-oriented tone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader,” “public-sector communications,” and the capability list repeat the subtitle and Core Competencies.
- “AI-enabled user experiences” is vague and overlaps with stronger, more specific project language elsewhere (“AI-enabled search”).
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and focused on the highest-value leadership areas rather than repeating detailed capabilities.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more executive-level phrases with consistent structure; e.g. “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Prioritize the most distinctive and recent strengths: enterprise web modernization, governance/editorial systems, analytics infrastructure, AI-enabled search, workflow automation, and multimedia operations.
- Consider replacing “Advocacy and public-sector communications” with “Public-sector digital communications” for cleaner phrasing and better alignment with the CV headline.
- Possible rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Public-sector digital communications • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications operations” and “Advocacy and public-sector communications” substantially overlap with the header and Topline Skills.
- This section should stay broad; avoid repeating tool-level detail already covered in Technical + IT.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening the wording and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more additive and less like a second summary.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Rename to “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one sharp line with parallel verb structure.
- Add scope, audience, or outcome where possible (for example: legislative content discovery, campaign growth, conference engagement, recurring advocacy cadence).
- Tighten phrasing: use “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” and “10-by-20-foot” for style consistency.
- Consider this rewrite format: “AI Hybrid Search — Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat to improve policy discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider emphasizing similarly unique projects here.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear relevance to your headline, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the “Recent Projects” section and prior NACo work. Tighten it around scope, seniority, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship initiatives.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform strategy, content operations, and enterprise web improvements.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-focused lines; combine systems/workflows/analytics and governance/usability/ops rather than listing adjacent functions separately.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: size of web properties, number of stakeholders/publishers supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy/engagement gains, or workflow time saved.
- Example phrasing: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery experiences” and “Built Drupal campaign microsites and modular storytelling components for member-facing advocacy campaigns.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current bullets duplicate the footer project summaries; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the build details.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” also echoes the NACo Director role; emphasize what is new in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Prioritize the most distinctive wins first: website migration, analytics stack expansion, and in-house studio build.
- Make bullets more outcome-led and parallel, e.g.:
- “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia content.”
- “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting infrastructure to improve performance visibility and decision-making.”
- If possible, add measurable results for email/social growth, production volume, budget size, team size, or efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version higher-level and more strategic.
- Governance/publishing standards language also appears elsewhere; tie it to enterprise-scale change or specific operational results.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier digital/media role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel ownership, and systems/process improvements that set up the later scale-up.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and make them outcome-led: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add stronger systems language: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership language.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered in the Director of Digital Media role; keep this entry centered on execution and workflow building.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tightened to emphasize higher-level leadership strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy and platform governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy content strategy
- Audience-centered planning and message architecture

- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “for high-volume, multi-stakeholder organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “governance,” and “multi-channel communications” are already echoed in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version if trimming.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool dump to a sharper capability line: “Drupal platform leadership • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level and relevance: “Drupal (primary enterprise CMS) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, group by strength: “Enterprise CMS: Drupal, SharePoint, Power Pages • Publishing platforms: WordPress, GitHub Pages”
- Prioritize recent/high-impact tools first; Drupal should clearly lead given the 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work.
- If you can substantiate it elsewhere, add a qualifier such as “Drupal 10” or “enterprise web publishing” for specificity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, and SharePoint.
- Consider deleting GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project; it reads lighter-weight than the rest.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, AI search, analytics, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Replace with a tighter list: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers unless they matter technically; “HTML5/CSS3” adds little value on a leadership CV.
- If space allows, add one short qualifier for impact/context, e.g. “for Drupal builds, analytics instrumentation, automation, and lightweight serverless tooling.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; consider keeping detail here and shortening the Topline version.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid re-adding it in this item unless tied to a specific tool.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so this item should be tighter and more differentiated.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by function to show judgment, not just familiarity: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: “Used to build content operations, cross-team planning, and lightweight automation workflows.”
- Keep only tools you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; drop weaker/older platforms if they don’t support current positioning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; if space is tight, prioritize actual workflow/automation platforms over basic comms apps.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it’s currently just a vendor list. Make it sharper by signaling platform category and aligning with the stronger, recent NACo/email experience.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope/context in brief: Enterprise email automation • Newsletter distribution • Member engagement campaigns
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest platform experience first; if Higher Logic or Dynamics powered NACo’s newsletters, place that tool first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; keep this section tool-focused, not responsibility-focused
- Avoid repeating “multi-channel communications” language already covered in Core Competencies and multiple roles

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item currently duplicates the “Topline Skills” analytics section almost exactly. It would be stronger if tightened and reframed around higher-value capabilities rather than a flat tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics, Measurement & Optimization
- Replace with a more capability-led line: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, and Microsoft Clarity • KPI design and leadership reporting • SEO/performance analysis • Experimentation and conversion optimization
- Consider dropping “Dashboarding” since reporting/leadership reporting already conveys it more professionally.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie to impact in experience bullets instead of here (e.g., analytics infrastructure supporting strategic decision-making).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly redundant with “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; keep one more tool-focused and the other more strategic, or remove one.
- “A/B testing” may overstate depth unless supported by a work-experience example.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the next NACo role. Make it more execution-focused and tie it to foundational team-building, platform work, and content production with any available scale metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and support day-to-day operations across web, email, social and video.”
- Replace soft phrasing like “high-impact” with concrete outputs: mention number/frequency of livestreams, weekly video updates, campaign launches, or audience reach if known.
- Clarify the website contribution: “Supported a major website refresh” could become “Helped execute a major website refresh, improving publishing workflows and content delivery.”
- Tighten management language: “provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate” → “mentored a digital media associate on production and publishing workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Workflow improvement language also appears in later NACo roles; frame this as the foundation stage.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around concrete outputs so it complements—rather than repeats—the later digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize ownership and firsts: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program priorities; produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add 1 measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience/downloads, stakeholder groups served, or project deliverables completed.
- Consider trimming “supporting organizational programs and policy work” and “contributed to” language, which reads passive.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad multimedia/content production language already covered in later NACo roles unless this item adds a distinct “first podcast” or research/innovation angle.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here; later roles already show progression into team and platform leadership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it mixes software with capabilities and repeats multimedia themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize tools and only the most distinctive production capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Broadcast/livestream studio production • Podcast planning and production”
- Keep this section tool-forward; use clearer, more professional phrasing than “Livestream studio workflows.”
- If possible, add specificity only if true: “multi-camera livestream production,” “audio editing/mastering,” or “studio recording workflows.”
- Consider dropping one lower-value item if space is tight; the strongest differentiators are Premiere Pro, Audition, livestream studio production, and podcast production.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Podcast production” overlaps with older NACo experience; keep it only if you want to preserve breadth.
- “Livestream studio workflows” overlaps with Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same wording elsewhere.
